CDKN2A homozygous deletion is also a classic co-driver in glioblastoma with high confidence. No targeted therapy exists, so no therapeutic relevance. 

PDGFRA amplification is another recurrent alteration in glioblastoma, so co-driver with high confidence. Again, no approved targeted therapies. 

The two EGFR missense mutations (p.A289V and p.E160K) are less clear. They're not classic oncogenic hotspots in glioblastoma like EGFRvIII. Without glioblastoma-specific evidence, these should be VUS with low confidence. No therapeutic relevance.
